reasoning: Original GRID24 row/column traversal, UV formula, point formula and triangle index order retained. Templates contain topology/neutral points/UV-only anatomy, not live pose or GPU state.
Points and units are duplicated into each instance, indices duplicated into each new ArrayMesh. bounds still used dynamically by deformation; no per-instance mesh or pose shared.

Kind-specific weights built by original PlainsRevisionWeights constructor and only shared after array.make_read_only. Actual production writes to weight fields occur only in constructor; consumers read them.
Existing _weights_kind invalidation still switches to the matching anatomy; rest cache keys/material refresh/draw call remain unchanged.
@static_unload limits static cache to script lifetime, and contents have no Node/actor/world references or back-reference to Skin. Strict engine teardown still needs actual verification.

New tests run actual CanvasItem draws and compare canonical vertex bytes, verify two rigs share weight objects while ArrayMesh instances differ, and mutate one instance point array then verify peer/later-template bodies unchanged.
limitations: Array.make_read_only is shallow: it prevents array structural edits, not mutation of RefCounted weight object fields. Safety is actual read-only consumer discipline, not deep immutability.

Custom external mutation of private _units or weight fields is not an admitted tested contract; current source consumers only read these. No new broad mutation API should be introduced without revisiting cache invalidation.
Mesh-instance isolation checks are not GPU pixel readback/device rendering evidence.
No engine/browser/benchmark run by reviewer, no final performance/frame-time claim.
